sources.citation: Aunio, Lotta & Axel Fleisch (eds.) 2019. Linguistic Diversity Research among Speakers of isiNdebele and Sindebele in South Africa. Studia Orientalia 120. Helsinki: Finnish Oriental Society. 331 pp. (whole volume, incl. Fleisch & Aunio 'Introduction', Jallow et al. 'Language dynamics among speakers of Sindebele', Schulz et al. 'Click variation and reacquisition in two South African Ndebele varieties', Aunio et al. 'Nominal tone in isiNdebele').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on Sindebele stress/accent. The only prosodic chapter (nominal tone, penultimate lengthening) is on isiNdebele (Southern, sout3270). For Sindebele the volume treats sociolinguistics and click loss, and states (p. 216) that 'The phonological system of Sindebele has been described by Ziervogel (1959) and later Msimang (1989) and Skhosana (2009)'; the introduction calls Ziervogel 1959 a 'short grammar sketch' and notes Sindebele tone is unanalysed.

sources.citation: Skhosana, Philemon Buti 2009. The linguistic relationship between Southern and Northern Ndebele. DLitt thesis, University of Pretoria. xvi+450 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Chapter 3 ('Phonological differences between Southern and Northern Ndebele') covers vowel and consonant systems, Ziervogel's vowel observations, nasal compounds; no suprasegmental/stress/accent section. Only incidental tone remarks (e.g. demonstrative suffix -a 'long in length and that carries a high tone').

sources.citation: Wilkes, Arnett 2007. The multilingual composition of Northern Ndebele. In M.J. Mojalefa (ed.), Rabadia Ratšhatšha: Studies in African language literature, linguistics, translation and lexicography, pp. 157ff. Stellenbosch: SUN Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Silent on stress. Sections on 'the multilingual character of the Northern Ndebele sound system/phonology/morphology' are segmental (bilabial fricative, velar affricates, Venda/Swati sounds, nasal compounds); no mention of stress, tone or length.

sources.citation: PanSALB 2001. Northern Ndebele (SiNdebele) orthography and spelling rules. PanSALB Occasional Papers. Pretoria: Pan South African Language Board.

sources.note: Official revised sound system of Northern Ndebele (cited by Wilkes 2007 and Skhosana 2009); orthography documents sometimes state whether length/stress is marked and where it falls.

sources.citation: Msimang, Christian Themba 1989. Some phonological aspects of the Tekela Nguni dialects. DLitt et Phil thesis, University of South Africa, Pretoria.

sources.note: Comparative phonology of the Tekela Nguni dialects including Sumayela Ndebele (Msimang coined the name); likely has a prosody/length section per dialect. UNISA repository normally serves digitised theses but was deliberately shut down on the day of search.

sources.citation: Ziervogel, Dirk 1959. A Grammar of Northern Transvaal Ndebele (a Tekela Nguni dialect spoken in the Pietersburg and Potgietersrus districts of the Transvaal). Pretoria: J.L. van Schaik. x+227 pp.

sources.note: The only full grammar of Sumayela Ndebele (tone-marked, descriptive, on the plan of his Grammar of Swazi which has an explicit stress/length paragraph); the phonology chapter is where a statement on stress/penultimate length will be. Glottolog's Glottolog's most extensive description for sout2808.
